openings.claim: Clarifying the existing coloured tray tags' material identities may reduce shared-material omissions if ambiguous identification causes them. This evaluates a bounded probe; the eventual intervention remains unproven for all 60 complete, correctly assigned kits within 90 minutes and at most one distribution correction.
openings.delta: Add explicit material names and specified dimensions in pencil to the existing tags, if writable. Retain their identification function, all pattern quantities and dimensions, existing envelopes and supplies, exactly two volunteers, the existing table and the 90-minute ceiling.
openings.prediction: With matched pattern mixtures, clarified tags produce fewer wrong-material or wrong-dimension picks and fewer shared-material omissions than the original tags. They need not reduce crossing reaches, reveal unopened stock or make assigned patterns apparent on envelope exteriors.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative explanation is quantity loss during picking or envelope filling despite correct material identification. It predicts unchanged omissions under clearer identity tags. O4 does not discriminate because its pattern mixture is unknown.
openings.defeat: Correct identification in both conditions, with omissions occurring during filling and no reduction under clarified tags, would defeat the proposed identification explanation.
openings.probe: Within one session, have the two volunteers assemble twelve kits per tag condition with the same pattern mixture and exchanged condition order. Count these toward the intended 60. Tally identification mistakes, omissions, exact contents and elapsed time including tag preparation and checks. Keep all work on the existing table and end by 90 minutes. Record whether all 60 ultimately meet the distribution criterion; a successful 24-kit comparison alone cannot establish that outcome for participants or assemblers.
assumptions: Existing tags accept legible pencil text without replacement materials.
Matched pattern mixtures can be allocated from existing supplies.
Supply packets and verification work fit the table; their footprint is unconfirmed.
Identification contributes materially to omissions; the synthetic stipulations establish no tested benefit.
